title: Read an environment status honestly
summary: An environment represents a place where an application runs, such as a preview or production site. A deployment record links a version to that place.
introduction: An environment represents a place where an application runs, such as a preview or production site. A deployment record links a version to that place. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Explain read an environment status honestly
Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: An environment represents a place where an application runs, such as a preview or production site. A deployment record links a version to that place.

blocks.code:
Environment: preview
Deployment: commit abc123 from the example project
Checks: page loads and search works
Limit: this status does not describe production
blocks.title: Read an environment status honestly

blocks.text: The record identifies which version was put in which place. Our example is a written plan and does not deploy anything.

items: Read the example from top to bottom. Point to the part that uses the new idea.
List one check before calling a preview ready for review.
Explain what changed in your own words. Check the example again if you get stuck.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: A green deployment job does not prove the running page behaves correctly; inspect it.
For more detail later, use this [GitLab further reading](https://docs.gitlab.com/tutorials/).
